subject: Request: custom uptime rider & evidence appendix for CloudHealth enterprise MSA
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@cloudhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudHealth Procurement <procurement@cloudhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: uptime / P99 latency commitments & evidence for enterprise MSA

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a productive internal alignment session and Procurement asked me to surface two items we'd like to include in the order form / MSA appendix before we finalize:

1) A dedicated uptime rider: CloudHealth needs a written commitment to 99.95% monthly availability for critical inference endpoints referenced in the SOW.
2) Latency guardrail: For our 256-token median workloads, we'd like a P99 latency target <= 350ms with a clear credit schedule for breaches.

Procurement also wants to see the evidence appendix — runbook excerpts, on-call escalation path, and a short evidence matrix mapping what you'll provide (SOC 2 report, audit logs, latency dashboards). If you can provide draft order form language and an evidence checklist, Procurement can run the legal review in parallel with our payments team.

Can you send a proposed uptime rider draft and an evidence matrix this week? We have a planned sign-off window the week of Sep 20.

Thanks,
Sara Liu
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudHealth Inc.

Attachment: (none)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: uptime / P99 latency commitments & evidence for enterprise MSA

Sara — really appreciate the clear asks.

We can accommodate a tailored uptime rider and a P99 latency guardrail for the endpoints you specify. To keep things operationally sustainable for both sides, I propose this approach:

- Draft an "Uptime & Performance Rider" that pins 99.95% monthly availability for named inference routes and includes a phased credit schedule for sustained breaches.
- For latency, propose a P99 <= 350ms for the "production" route under steady-state traffic up to an agreed baseline TPS; include a measured exclusion for scheduled maintenance and region-level incidents.
- Provide an evidence appendix with: SOC 2 attestation link, 90-day latency dashboards (per-route P50/P95/P99), runbook excerpts (incident notification SLA, on-call rota), and an evidence matrix mapping each procurement ask to a document/artefact.

I'm attaching a preliminary draft rider and an evidence matrix to get us started (see attachments). Ben — looped in to confirm any commercial implications for credits/price. Kimberly — can you weigh in on procurement/evidence expectations?

Next steps:
- We will send a redline-ready rider (docx) and a completed evidence matrix by Fri EOD PT.
- If CloudHealth can flag any specific routes (API keys or model IDs) that must be covered, we'll bake them into the order form language.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft-uptime-rider.docx, evidence-matrix.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: uptime / P99 latency commitments & evidence for enterprise MSA

Forwarding for visibility. Quick commercial notes:

- 99.95% baseline is within the realm of our Dedicated tier SLAs, but if CloudHealth wants that across multiple regions or with strict latency credits we should confirm reserved capacity or a throughput commitment.
- Credits: recommend a stepped schedule (e.g., 0.5% credit for month <99.95, 1.0% for <99.8, escalated caps) rather than unlimited credits.
- Latency commitments are trickier — we can provide P99 targets for a named route with a baseline throughput cap. If they need global P99 across multiple routes, we'll need uplift pricing.

Olga — happy to sync with you on a short call if you want to co-present options.

Ben
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Please review: proposed uptime rider language for CloudHealth (attached redline)

David — attaching a redline of the rider (redline-uptime-rider.docx) and the evidence matrix. CloudHealth asked for order form language they can push through internal legal. Key asks:

- 99.95% monthly availability for the specified production endpoints
- P99 latency <= 350ms for the named route, with an explicit baseline TPS and exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure
- A clear credit schedule tied to monthly availability and a separate credit mechanism for latency breaches
- Evidence appendix that references our SOC 2 (link), 90-day latency dashboards, and the on-call runbook excerpt (which we don't want to publish fully but can produce under NDA)

Please review and recommend:
- Whether our exclusion language is sufficiently protective (scheduled maintenance window, degradation due to customer misuse, DDOS mitigations)
- Any redlines to the credit cap / recovery process

Thanks — can you return comments by EOD Mon so we can send to CloudHealth Tue morning?

Olga

Attachments: redline-uptime-rider.docx, evidence-matrix.xlsx
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Please review: proposed uptime rider language for CloudHealth (attached redline)

Thanks for the deck, Olga. I reviewed the redline and recommend the following changes (high level):

- Tighten the definition of "available" to explicitly reference successful 2xx responses for named endpoints (and document the measurement method and time buckets).
- Add an exclusion for client-side induced latency (e.g., malformed payloads, unsupported tokenization causing retries).
- Cap aggregate credits for the term at a percentage of the annual contract value (suggest 6%) to limit open-ended exposure.
- Require 72-hour notice for scheduled maintenance that could affect availability (except emergency patches).
- For the latency SLA, include a clause where we measure P99 on a sampling window and allow a one-month remedy period before credits apply, to avoid transient measurement noise.

I incorporated these recommendations in the attached redline and added comment flags where I think we should offer a mildly enhanced remedy in exchange for an annual commit (e.g., improved credits / guaranteed regional failover).

If this looks good, we can produce a clean rider and a short cover letter explaining the evidence artifacts we'll provide under NDA.

David Kim
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@cloudhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, CloudHealth Procurement <procurement@cloudhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: uptime / P99 latency commitments & evidence for enterprise MSA — proposed rider + evidence appendix

Sara — attaching the updated rider and evidence matrix reflecting our legal team's input. Summary of what we're proposing:

- Uptime: 99.95% monthly availability for the named production endpoints; measurement defined as successful 2xx responses across the measurement window; standard exclusions apply.
- Latency: P99 <= 350ms on the named route measured on a 30-day rolling window; a one-month remedial window before credits trigger.
- Credits: stepped schedule with a maximum annual credit cap at 6% of the contract annual value; separate latency credit schedule.
- Evidence: SOC 2 link (will provide latest report under NDA), per-route 90-day latency dashboards (shareable view), and runbook excerpts for incident notification.

Attachments: redline-uptime-rider.docx (with legal comments), evidence-matrix.xlsx (maps requests to artifacts), and a short cover letter we can route into DocuSign.

If CloudHealth is comfortable with the cap and remedial window we proposed, we can produce a clean rider and route it for signature. Otherwise, happy to hop on a 30-minute call with Procurement + Legal to walk through tradeoffs.

Next steps:
- If OK, please confirm the specific routes (API keys / model IDs) you want covered and we will produce the final order form language.
- If you prefer an in-person legal deep-dive, Ben and David are available Wed/Thu this week.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Olga Petrov
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline-uptime-rider.docx, evidence-matrix.xlsx, cover-letter.pdf
